chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abū Ja'far, from 'Alī ibn al-Hakam, from Abān, from 'Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abī 'Abd Allah, from Abū 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who becomes junub in a garment, and he has no other than it, and he is not able to wash it. He said: “He prays in it.”

Discussion concerning these reports is from several angles. One of them is that in none of them is it stated which prayer he prays in it; so when this is not specified in it, we interpret it as the funeral prayer, because the funeral prayer is among that which a person may perform even if his garment is not tahir, just as it is permissible that his own state not be tahir.

And another possibility is that it is permissible for him to pray, except that when water is found it becomes obligatory upon him to wash it and repeat the prayer. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: garment or clothing worn for prayer
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes in a state of janabah

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he becomes junub in his only garment and cannot wash it before prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the case of a person who becomes junub in his only garment and cannot wash it, with the Imam عليه السلام stating that he prays in it. The accompanying discussion presents juristic ways of understanding the report, including applying it to salat al-janazah or allowing the prayer temporarily with later washing and repetition once water is available.
